newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest hydropower dam inflows increasing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest hydropower dam inflows increasing.

text.p: Inflows to hydropower projects in the Pacific Northwest are picking up speed, but a start date for voluntary spill at Columbia River dams has not been finalized, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers said Monday.
But the higher flows have resulted in some uncontrolled spill, noted a Corps spokesman.
At The Dalles dam on the Columbia, for instance, inflows on Sunday averaged 320,000 cubic feet per second (cfs), compared with 270,000 cfs late last week.
Spill at The Dalles on Sunday ranged from 24,000 cfs to 190,000 cfs, according to the Corps.
Sunday inflows at Bonneville Dam averaged 320,000 cfs, up from 285,000 cfs late last week.

Under the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) Biological Opinion, up to 64 percent of discharge from Columbia River projects will be spilled around-the-clock as an aid to the spring migration of salmon and other fish.
Corps officials and the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) expect to meet today to iron out an exact date for Columbia River spill to start.
Fish interests made a formal request for spill implementation on Friday, noted the Corps spokesman.
On the Snake River, where voluntary spill was implemented on April 10, inflows to Lower Granite Dam averaged 156,000 cfs on Sunday, compared with lows of 80,000 cfs in mid-April.
